# Rune A native GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for macOS, Windows, Linux and the web, with its own renderer, text, layout and springs. Every app can run headless, so an agent can render to PNG, dump the element tree and drive it with scripted input.

```rust fn view(s: &State, _: &mut Cx) -> El { let t = tok::theme(true); let label = text(if s.on { "Lights on" } else { "Lights off" }) .font(type_::TITLE).color(t.text); let knob = el().key("knob").size(18.0, 18.0).radius(9.0).fill(t.knob) .absolute(if s.on { 18.0 } else { 2.0 }, 2.0); let switch = el().key("switch").role("switch").label("Lights").checked(s.on) .focusable(true).size(38.0, 22.0).radius(11.0) .fill(if s.on { tok::accent(0, true) } else { t.control_off }) .motion(motion::SNAPPY) .on_press(|s: &mut State| s.on = !s.on) .child(knob); col().w_full().h_full().center().gap(16.0).fill(t.bg).child(label).child(switch) } ``` ## Use it with your agent Give your coding agent this repo. Have it start from [`examples/hello`](examples/hello) and [`crates/rune/README.md`](crates/rune/README.md), then check its own work headlessly by rendering PNGs and inspecting the element tree. > Build me a with Rune (github.com/anomalyco/rune). Start from examples/hello and check your work headlessly. ## Add it ```toml rune = { git = "https://github.com/anomalyco/rune", rev = "" } ``` Rune is pre-release. Pin a rev of `dev`; `dev` is never rewritten. On Windows, the MSVC toolchain (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, rustup's default) needs only the Visual Studio C++ build tools rustup asks for. The GNU toolchain (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`) also needs MinGW-w64's binutils on `PATH`: `windows-link` (under `parking_lot`, `libloading`, `windows-core` and `windows-sys`, so under every Windows UI crate) imports with `raw-dylib`, rustc makes those import libraries with `dlltool` on GNU targets, and the `dlltool` in rustup's `rust-mingw` can't run without an `as` it doesn't ship ([rust-lang/rust#140704](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/140704)). Without binutils the build stops at `windows-result` with `error calling dlltool 'dlltool.exe': program not found`. Install [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org), run `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-binutils`, and put `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` on `PATH` (or build with `RUSTFLAGS=-Cdlltool=C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\dlltool.exe`). [Docs](crates/rune/README.md) · [Components](crates/rune-kit/README.md) · [Examples](examples) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## Contributing We don't take pull requests. Have your agent [open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/rune/issues) describing the bug or idea, and our agents usually turn it around fast. MIT, © Anomaly.

# Exact **The all-platform app framework. Agent native. Built for speed. No compromises.** Exact is an **all-platform** framework for building real apps on the web, iOS, macOS, Android, and Linux — with Windows in active development, plus tvOS, watchOS, Android TV, and the terminal. Exact is not a "cross-platform" framework. Cross-platform tools usually trade away each platform's strengths to maintain a lowest common denominator. Exact takes the opposite approach: build something **excellent on every platform on its own terms** — real DOM on the web, real UIKit on iOS, real AppKit on macOS, hardware-accelerated Material 3 rendering with native Android views on Android, and direct GPU/CPU rendering on Linux and Windows. Being **all-platform** is simply the side effect of getting every platform right from one source. Everything in Exact is built around three priorities: 1. **[Agent Native](#1-agent-native)** — Built from the ground up so coding agents can build, run, see, operate, and verify real apps on every platform through one deterministic loop. 2. **[Speed is King](#2-speed-is-king)** — 100 ms cold starts, 100 ms edit-to-present reloads, zero app JavaScript before first pixel, and a ~20 KB web runtime, held to hard budgets. 3. **[No Compromises — Build Exactly What You Want](#3-no-compromises--build-exactly-what-you-want)** — Native platform controls with zero tells when you leave presentation unsaid; full creative control over layout, motion, graphics, shaders, and native platform objects whenever you want it. > [!NOTE] > Exact is pre-1.0 and changes daily. There is no packaged release, API stability guarantee, or backwards-compatibility layer yet — you build from a checkout of this repository.
Web iOS macOS
The browser's own DOM and CSS UIKit views, native controls, and the system tab bar AppKit views and native controls
One source, three platforms, captured by Exact's agent driver. content.readme:
HatchZip

Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch,
so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive.

hatchzip.dev | Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing

HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a desktop app and a command line tool. It extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, for when there is not enough disk space to extract an archive next to itself, such as a large game download on a nearly full disk. Download it from [hatchzip.dev](https://hatchzip.dev). A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`, RAR volume sets and split archives. ### Get it > [!IMPORTANT] > HatchZip is only distributed from this repository's [releases](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) and its site, [hatchzip.dev](https://hatchzip.dev). Other sites using the name, such as hatchzip.com, are not affiliated with this project. No coding needed. **[Download for Windows](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe)** (Windows 10 and 11), or for [macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS (Intel)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) and [Linux](#installation). 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. 2. Right-click the archive, choose **HatchZip**, then **Extract here**. On Windows 11 the menu is under **Show more options**. To pick the destination folder first, choose **Extract files…** instead. 3. Or open HatchZip from the Start menu, open the archive, and choose **Extract**. HatchZip shows whether the files will fit before it changes anything. The archive is used up as the files come out, so when it finishes, only the extracted files are left. **Extract here** puts an archive with one folder or one file at its top next to the archive. An archive with several files or folders at its top goes into a new folder named after it, so its files never mix with what is already there. The progress window closes when the extraction completes; to keep it open, clear **Close the progress window when extraction completes** in the app's Settings menu. To keep the archive when there is room for both, choose **Extract here (keep archive)** in the right-click menu. content.readme:
# CHIMERA

A physical-modeling voice synthesizer in the browser. Every sound comes from a simulated
airway (lungs, vocal folds or syrinx, a branched vocal tract, lips, nose), not from samples.
The engine is Rust, compiled to WebAssembly for an AudioWorklet; the same code runs natively
for tests and the `chimera` CLI.

## Vision & scope

1. **One instrument**: a physically modeled voice (lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth). No
   samples, no neural audio.
2. **The web app is the primary surface**: anyone should be able to make songs in it without
   an LLM's help. Mobile is the likely next surface. The plugin (CLAP/VST3/AU) still ships, but
   it's secondary.
3. **As realistic as we can make it**: the main push is to see how close the simulation gets to
   a real voice. The robotic, Vocaloid-like sound people like today stays playable as a preset
   ([#93](https://github.com/jamesondh/chimera-vocal-synth/issues/93)).
4. **Languages enter through one shared front-end design**, not one-off hacks. Each needs a
   native speaker's check and must leave English unchanged.
5. **The design language (the vector display) is settled**; the look within it can still evolve.
6. **Nothing copyrighted in git**; MIT; a deterministic, real-time-safe engine.
7. **Not now**: a DAW or sequencer, a light theme, MPE, multi-voice dialogue, translating the
   interface (the voice speaks and sings many languages; the labels stay in English).

## What it does

- **Play**: drag the tongue, lips and jaw in a live cutaway of the head; vowel pad, encoders,
  computer keyboard and Web MIDI.
- **Speak**: English text (CMUdict with a letter-to-sound fallback), Turkish text (EN/TR) or
  IPA, turned into gestures and prosody, with the gestural score and a consonant chart on screen.
  In IPA mode a notice under the box lists the symbols and marks the voice doesn't say
  (`chimera render speech` prints the same as warnings).
- **Sing**: type words and the **Sing** button sings them to a tune picked by its mood, each line
  fitted to a phrase of it (Tempo and Key on the Voice screen); **Record video** sings it again into a
  9:16 clip to share. The keys sing the same words a syllable at a time, legato or not, onto a
  pitch roll; consonants land before the beat. Lyrics can be English, Turkish (chosen with EN/TR:
  Latin script can't tell them apart), Korean (Hangul: one block per note, with Korean sound
  rules) or Russian; each language is a front end
  ([docs/language-front-ends.md](docs/language-front-ends.md)).
- **Beatbox**: pads and a step sequencer, every drum an articulatory gesture.
- **Bestiary**: songbird (two-voice syrinx), seal, alligator and elephant.
- **Duet** (`?show=<id>`): two 3D heads replay a pre-rendered song.

Male, female and child bodies blend continuously. Everything on screen animates from live
engine state: pressure in the airway, airflow, the vocal folds, spectra and formants.

## Run it

Needs Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, and Bun.

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # builds the wasm, then Vite on 127.0.0.1:5317
bun run test       # wasm build, cargo test --workspace, bun test tests
```

The AudioWorklet needs a secure context, so open it on localhost or over HTTPS (for example
`tailscale serve`). Vercel builds it with `vercel.json`.

Offline renders and measurement:

```sh
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- render speech|text|song|notes|beatbox|creature|vowels …
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- diagnose       # nasal leakage, formants, bandwidths, pitch
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- compare csd    # against a real singer (docs/csd-comparison.md)
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- compare tsp    # against 23 real speakers (docs/speech-comparison.md)
bun tools/spectrogram.ts in.wav out.png
bun tools/musicxml-to-notes.ts score.mxl P1 --out p1.json   # a score's part → `render notes` melody
```

## Docs

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the acoustic model (FDTD airway, sources,
  anatomy, gestures), and its [references and credits](docs/architecture.md#references-and-credits).
- [docs/rust-engine.md](docs/rust-engine.md): the engine's real-time and determinism contract,
  and the browser boundary.
- [docs/ui-redesign.md](docs/ui-redesign.md) and [docs/mockups/](docs/mockups/): the vector
  display look.
- [docs/csd-comparison.md](docs/csd-comparison.md): scoring the voice against the Children's
  Song Dataset.
- [docs/speech-comparison.md](docs/speech-comparison.md): scoring the speech against real
  speakers, phone by phone (the TSP speech database).
- [docs/russian.md](docs/russian.md): how Russian text is read, and what is approximate.
- [docs/turkish.md](docs/turkish.md): how Turkish text is read: k, g and l, ğ, stress.
- [docs/hill-climb/](docs/hill-climb/): the rules and log for tuning the voice one measured
  step at a time.

Contributing: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Agents: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## License

content.readme:
Airhand

High-performance, low-latency remote desktop
QUIC transport · hardware encoding and decoding · up to 120 fps
Windows · macOS · Linux · Android · browser

English · 简体中文

--- Airhand is a **high-performance, low-latency** remote desktop: the screen is encoded on the GPU (AV1 / HEVC / H.264) at up to 120 fps and sent over QUIC; when the network slows down it skips to the latest frame instead of letting lag pile up; and the mouse pointer is drawn locally, so it moves without delay. The same program is both the **host** (the device being controlled) and the **controller** (the device you control it from). The two sides meet through a **relay server** that you deploy yourself. It's small, and Docker Compose deploys it with one command. Enter the other side's 6-digit **control code** to connect. > [!NOTE] > **Work in progress (0.3.1).** Build the relay, clients and web service from the same v10 revision; earlier builds cannot be mixed. Video uses one QUIC stream per frame. [Protocol versions](docs/development.md#protocol-versions) ## Performance Every stage from capture to display is built for low latency: - **Hardware encoding and decoding**: the host encodes on the GPU (NVENC / Quick Sync / AMF, VideoToolbox, MediaCodec) in low-latency mode without B-frames; the controller decodes on the GPU (WebCodecs / MediaCodec). Measured with a 4K screen streamed at 1080p, hardware AV1 encoding takes about 7 ms per frame (RTX graphics card) - **The best format**: AV1 > HEVC > H.264, automatically picking the most efficient format both sides support; scaling and color conversion use SIMD, and all buffers are reused - **No lag build-up**: the host limits the bytes in flight (≈ bitrate × (RTT + 50 ms)) and skips to the latest frame on a slow network; the bitrate follows the measured queueing delay and bandwidth on every acknowledgement, backing off within a few hundred milliseconds and recovering gradually - **Direct path**: besides the relay, the two ends punch a direct path through their NATs (on the same LAN, or whenever the NAT isn't symmetric), so video and audio stop detouring through the server; the lower-latency path is picked automatically, and if the direct path breaks the session falls back to the relay without dropping - **QUIC + BBR**: BBR congestion control is steadier than Cubic on lossy networks such as Wi-Fi or long-distance links; control messages, audio and video are queued separately, so mouse input and pings never wait behind a large frame; the relay only forwards bytes and never parses the video - **Loss doesn't stall the picture**: each frame travels on its own QUIC stream, so a lost packet only holds up that frame. A frame that keeps not arriving is abandoned (no more retransmitting stale data) and the encoder continues from a long-term reference frame the controller already has (reference invalidation) instead of sending a large keyframe (Windows H.264, NVIDIA AV1; other encoders send a keyframe) - **Decode and show**: the decoder runs in low-latency mode, and each frame is drawn to a desynchronized canvas as soon as it's decoded, without waiting for vsync - **Local pointer**: the remote cursor's shape is mirrored locally, and moving it happens locally - **Low bandwidth**: no frames are sent while the screen is still, so an idle desktop uses almost nothing; sessions that aren't on screen drop to 5 fps See [How it works → Video](docs/architecture.md#video) for details. ## Features - **Windows system service**: the lock screen, the sign-in screen and UAC prompts can be seen and controlled, and the computer can be reached after boot, before anyone signs in - **Fixed control codes**: they survive restarts, upgrades and even server restarts until you change them yourself - **Console**: browser-style tabs to control several computers at once, plus a multi-screen overview to watch them all. Computers you've connected to are saved and reconnect with one click; if one is offline, it connects as soon as it comes back - **Web console**: the controller can also run in Docker and be used from a browser, with nothing to install on the computer you control from - **Android**: control computers and phones from a phone as a trackpad or touchscreen, or share your own screen to get help (a device needs the pairing code shown on the phone the first time, and you're notified whenever one connects); watch on a TV with the remote - **Audio**: the host's system audio plays on the controller (Opus + adaptive jitter buffer), with optional A/V sync for watching videos. The other way, the controller can send its microphone to meeting apps and voice typing on Windows, macOS 14.2+ and Linux (PipeWire) hosts. Mac and Linux hosts publish **Airhand Microphone** while forwarding is on - **Handy tools**: two-way clipboard sync

content.readme:
Kensaku 検索

Fast, light, and efficient. Find anything on your computer.

Search 100,000 file names in milliseconds, with about 12 MB of metadata.
Search inside documents, images, and code too. Nothing leaves your machine.

Install · Why Kensaku · Features · Performance · MCP · Docs · Languages · Contribute

--- ## Find it the way you remember it You don't remember the filename. You remember what was in it. - The PDF about database indexing, saved as `notes-final-2.pdf`. - The log line from the failed deploy, somewhere in a folder of logs. - The screenshot with a CUDA error, which has no useful name at all. Type what you remember. Kensaku searches names, text inside files, and meaning, and shows the match with the words highlighted. Open it with Enter. ## What Kensaku does that the others don't Filename tools are everywhere. Reading *inside* your files — locally, instantly, and for free — is not. | | Kensaku | Everything | Listary | PowerToys Run | |---|---|---|---|---| | Filename search, milliseconds | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Full text inside PDF/DOCX/EPUB… | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Text inside screenshots & images (OCR) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Multilingual & CJK text (auto-tokenized) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Find by meaning ("the PDF about indexing") | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Natural-language time ("screenshots from last week") | ✅ | ❌ | partial | ❌ | | Your AI agents can search it (MCP) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Launcher behavior (summon, type, Enter) | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Open source (MIT) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | *Spotlight and Raycast are excellent but macOS-only; Alfred's content search and AI are paid tiers. Kensaku is one app, three platforms, free and MIT-licensed.* **Three things worth trying on day one:** 1. **Screenshot archaeology.** You know you saw that error in a screenshot. Kensaku read the pixels — search the error text. 2. **Describe, don't recall.** "big videos from last month" is a valid query. No filters to click. 3. **Give your AI agent eyes.** Claude or Cursor can search this same index over MCP — read-only, local, no cloud. ## Features **Fast** - Filename search across ~100,000 files in milliseconds on a warm cache. Method, hardware, and per-platform numbers are in [Performance](#performance). - Results update as you type. There is no separate search page. - Incremental indexing: changed files are picked up without rescanning the whole disk. - Closing the window keeps the index warm; reopening is instant. **Finds more** - Names, full text, fuzzy matches that tolerate typos, and meaning, in one search. - **Documents & Office**: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, EPUB, ODT/ODS/ODP, RTF, CSV/TSV, email (`.eml`, `.msg`), and plain text. - **Multilingual & CJK by default**: Custom unigram + bigram tokenizer for Chinese (Hanzi/Bopomofo), Japanese (Kanji/Kana), and Korean (Hangul), plus mixed-script boundary handling. Detailed breakdown in [docs/LANGUAGES.md](docs/LANGUAGES.md). - **50+ Code & Data Formats**: Rust, Python, TypeScript, Go, C/C++, Java, Shell, SQL, JSON, YAML, TOML, Dockerfile, and more. - **Images & OCR**: Text is read with PP-OCRv6 by default (bundled runtime; the ~6.1 MB model pack downloads once). content.readme: **vork is a 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents.** Agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03cfa020-be40-483a-89af-1ef77467b7a0 **One million birds, each on its own path.** 192 frames at 1080p rendered in 97 seconds on a single NVIDIA L4. Blender EEVEE at the same sample count is projected at 13–18 minutes. [How we measured](#million-birds-measured-movies-projected-blender-times) · [how it's made](examples/murmuration/) · [credits](examples/murmuration/CREDITS) - **Built for agents:** a small API that agents can extend with their own GPU programs. - **Fast:** 1.1–2.3× faster than EEVEE on default stills and movies, and about 8–11× on the bird flock. [Speed, with the qualifications](#speed-with-the-qualifications). - **Native GPU engine:** written in Rust and Slang, runs on Vulkan and Metal (Linux, Windows, macOS). - **No GPU needed:** render on Voyager's cloud GPUs with [vork cloud](https://voyager.so/vork/cloud). ## Paste this to your agent [Install vork](#install), then paste: > Run `vork init my-shot`, read `vork help`, render a preview and inspect the image. > Refine the camera and lighting before rendering at final quality. Read the > relevant help topic when you need a feature the first page doesn't explain. vork is written in Rust and Slang, with GPU rendering through Vulkan and Metal. An agent writes a scene, renders it, looks at the result and revises the code. There is no editor to drive. Most creative tools expose controls that a person can operate. An agent can also write a shader in the middle of a shot. vork gives it geometry, ray queries and GPU execution, then lets scene programs define materials, cameras, light propagation, simulation and compositing. Ordinary shots need only scene data; the programming hooks are there when the shot needs something unusual. Source-available and free during the research preview. ## Start here After [installing vork](#install), create a working project: ```sh vork init my-shot && cd my-shot vork skills add vork render scene.json --out render.png ``` Open `render.png`, change a colour or camera position in `scene.json`, and render again. The starter uses only bundled sphere, box and grid primitives: no downloads, no GPU needed to initialize. Use `vork init my-shot --language typescript` or `--language python` for editable `scene.ts` or `scene.py` alongside the ready-to-render JSON. The generated README explains regeneration and SDK requirements. Existing files are never overwritten. The default `std/final` profile is warmed by setup; use `--profile std/draft` for quicker previews. ## What you can make The examples include code, preparation commands and credits. Large downloaded assets and footage stay outside Git; the recipes fetch them or accept a local path. The images here are stills from these shots. basic_info.name: reylo
basic_info.description: Import .sql files into TypeScript with full type inference and zero codegen.

content.readme:
Import .sql files into your TypeScript code with full type inference

Read the docs →


If you have a file like this: ```sql -- get_author.sql select u.id, u.name, count(p.id)::int as post_count from users u left join posts p on p.user_id = u.id where u.id = :id::int group by u.id ``` You can import it directly from a TypeScript file like this: ```ts // main.ts import postgres from "postgres"; import getAuthor from "./get_author.sql"; const db = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL); const author = await getAuthor.run(db, { id: 1 }); // { id: number; name: string; post_count: number } | null ``` Reylo is powered by TypeScript [content mappers](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/pull/4712), introduced in [TypeScript 7.1](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-1-beta/) (currently in nightly builds), which let you dynamically define static types for external file types and integrate them directly into TypeScript compilation. Reylo is the perfect option for the agent era: - 💪 **The full power of SQL** — any syntax, function or operator your database supports - 🌵 **DRY** — no redundant hand-written types - 🎯 **Checked against your database** — a misspelled column is a type error - 🤖 **Agent-friendly** — DRY code is more maintainable for agents - 🧩 **Postgres, MySQL and SQLite** — Neon, PlanetScale, Cloudflare D1, Turso and more - 🔌 **Bring your own driver** — `pg`, postgres.js, `mysql2`, `better-sqlite3` and [more](#supported-drivers) - ⚡ **No codegen** — no generated files, no watcher ## Setup To install Reylo, you'll need: - **TypeScript 7.1 (currently in nightly builds).** The first release with content mappers. The `tsconfig.json` entry below needs a nightly from 2026-11-12 or later. - **Node 24 or later.** - **A running dev database.** Postgres, MySQL 8.0.38 or later, or a SQLite file: Reylo reads your current schema from it. Install Reylo, which brings its engine for your machine, and TypeScript 7.1: ```sh npm install reylo npm install -D typescript@next ``` Add Reylo to `tsconfig.json`, for `.sql` files and for its project file, `.reylo.yaml` or `.reylo.yml`: ```jsonc // tsconfig.json { "compilerOptions": { /* ... */ }, "contentMappers": [{ "package": "reylo" }] } ``` Then type-check with `--runExternalCode`, which lets `tsc` run content mappers: ```jsonc // package.json { "scripts": { "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit --runExternalCode" } } ``` Point Reylo at your dev database with `DATABASE_URL`, in your environment or in `.env`. Its scheme tells Reylo which database you use: ```sh # .env DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost:5432/app # or mysql://… or sqlite:./path/to/your.db, etc ``` To make `.sql` imports work at run time too, load Reylo where your code runs. On Node: ```sh node --env-file=.env --import reylo/register main.ts ``` For Bun, Nub, Vite, Next.js, esbuild, webpack, Rspack, Cloudflare Workers and Jest, add [the plugin for your setup](https://reylo.dev/#plugins), or copy its complete [example project](https://github.com/reylosql/reylo/tree/main/examples). To see the types as you type, set up [your editor](https://reylo.dev/#editors). To give your coding agent Reylo's rules for writing and running queries, install its skill: ```sh npx skills add reylosql/reylo --skill reylo ``` ## Usage Write a query in a `.sql` file, import it, and run it with your database driver: ```sql -- get_user.sql select id, name, email from users where id = :id::int ``` ```ts import getUser from "./get_user.sql"; const user = await getUser.run(db, { id: 1 }); // { id: number; name: string; email: string | null } | null ``` Name each parameter with a colon, and give it a type with a cast where the query doesn't pin one down. Pass `.run()` your driver's client: a pool, a client, or a connection or transaction taken from one

basic_info.description: 岛仔 Daozai：Rust 构建的 Windows 桌面信息岛。音乐歌词、邮件验证码、日程提醒、待办与 AI 额度，让重要信息轻轻出现在屏幕顶部。

content.readme:
# 岛仔 · Daozai **一座小岛，装下桌面日常。** Windows 桌面伙伴，把消息、音乐、日程、天气和 AI 额度放到手边。 [![最新版本](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai?color=7955b8&label=最新版本)](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai/releases/latest) [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%20%2F%2011-0078D4)](#下载安装) [![开源许可](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-3cbf91)](LICENSE) [![Rust 与 egui](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-egui-8b6ca8)](#从源码构建与参与开发) **[下载 Windows 版](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai/releases/latest)** · [使用指南](docs/USAGE.md) · [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md) · [反馈问题](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai/issues)
岛仔是一款开源的 Windows 桌面小工具。平时收起在屏幕边缘，鼠标靠近就展开；切歌、看日程、复制验证码、记一条待办，都能顺手完成。小岛里的伙伴会眨眼、打盹、喝水，也会跟着音乐唱歌。 你可以选刘海或胶囊，放在顶部、左侧或右侧，只保留自己需要的功能。岛仔使用 Rust 和 egui 构建，不依赖 Electron。 ## 微信里有新消息，看一眼岛边 ![微信和 QQ 未读：收起时显示图标，展开后点击切换对应窗口](docs/images/readme/notifications.webp) - **微信、QQ 未读提醒**：收起时亮起图标和红点，展开后在面板旁查看，点击切换到对应窗口。 - **微信多开分开看**：不同账号分别显示，点击对应账号的未读图标即可切换。 - **按需显示通知正文**：默认隐藏正文；开启预览后仍遮罩识别出的验证码。 - **微信提醒不读取聊天正文**：根据任务栏闪动提示新消息。微信缩在托盘时，可选开启「托盘一键唤起微信」。 开启方式：**设置 → 通知、邮箱与日程 → 通知**。微信开启「微信新消息提醒」；QQ 选择「只连接 QQ」，并在 QQ 中启用 Windows 系统通知。 ## 换个皮肤，也换个位置 ![五款皮肤：经典黑、奶油、毛玻璃浅色、毛玻璃深色、悬浮云；刘海和胶囊两种形态](docs/images/readme/appearance.webp) **五款皮肤 × 两种形态，自由搭配。** 经典黑、奶油、毛玻璃·浅、毛玻璃·深和「悬浮云」，都能搭配刘海或胶囊。毛玻璃透出身后的桌面；悬浮云随专辑封面换色，光晕跟着鼠标移动。 ![顶部、左侧和右侧停靠，以及侧边收起与展开状态](docs/images/readme/docking.webp) - **三边停靠**：顶部横向展开，左右侧边收起为竖向胶囊，靠近后从屏幕边缘展开。 - **大小与位置可调**：岛体大小支持 80%–140%；顶部可左右移动，侧边可上下调整。 - **OLED 像素偏移**（默认关闭）：收起静止时沿停靠边缓慢移动几个像素，帮助减轻 OLED 静态显示留下的痕迹。 - **多屏与自动避让**：跟随主屏或固定到指定显示器。前台浏览器或自定义应用的窗口遮住岛时，岛会收成贴边细线。切到插件浮窗时，如果名单里的宿主窗口仍遮住岛，岛会继续避让。 - **按习惯显示**：支持极简模式、12／24 小时制，以及功能页面开关与拖动排序。 在 **设置 → 常规 → 岛体外观／岛体显示** 中调整。岛上单行歌词目前支持顶部停靠。 ## 听歌时，歌词就在抬眼处 ![音乐播放控制、展开歌词与收起状态下的岛上单行歌词](docs/images/readme/music.webp) 播放、暂停、切歌、调节音量和拖动进度，都能在岛上操作。展开看歌词，也可以收起后只留一行歌词，让桌面继续做自己的事。 - 通过 Windows 媒体会话读取播放信息，并针对网易云音乐、QQ 音乐、酷狗、汽水音乐补充兼容。 - 网易云优先按歌曲 ID 找词，改善译名、合唱署名和 Live／Remix 等不同版本的匹配。 播放器需提供可用的媒体信息；歌词取决于歌曲元数据与歌词来源，个别歌曲或播放器版本可能无法显示。 ## 日程、待办和专注，放在一起 ![日历与会议安排、每周重复待办、番茄专注与饮水提醒](docs/images/readme/daily.webp) | 想做的事 | 岛仔能帮你 | | --- | --- | | 看今天的安排 | 月历与当日时间线，合并多个日历和正式邮件邀请，提前提醒会议 | | 记住每周的事 | 待办支持单次提醒、每周指定日期重复或每天重复；下一次到来时恢复为待办 | | 专心做一件事 | 专注与休息计时，收起时也能查看进度 | | 记得喝水 | 自定义每日目标、单次饮水量、提醒间隔与时段，记录错误可撤销 | 日历可接入 **飞书、钉钉、企业微信、iCloud、自定义 CalDAV 和兼容的 Exchange ActiveSync**，也能导入 `.ics` 文件。相同日程合并去重；支持全天、跨天和重复日程。 本机新建或导入的日程保存在本机；远程日历为只读同步。程序退出、电脑关机或睡眠期间无法持续提醒。 ## 文件先放岛上，刚复制的字也能找回 ![文件置物架与剪贴板历史：拖入文件、重新复制文字、固定常用内容](docs/images/readme/shelf.webp) **文件置物架**：拖入文件临时收集，点击打开、定位原文件，或拖出到其他应用。移除记录不会删除原文件。 **文字剪贴板**：找回最近复制的 30 条文字，点一下重新复制，常用内容可以固定。历史保存在本机，重启后仍可查看；可在 **设置 → 待办与置物 → 剪贴板** 中关闭。密码管理器标记为敏感的内容不记录。 ## 验证码少切一次窗口，邮件也能直接读 ![验证码大卡点击复制与邮件正文阅读](docs/images/readme/mail.webp) 连接多个邮箱，在岛上查看来信、识别验证码并点击复制。邮件支持正文阅读与独立全文窗口，网页链接交给默认浏览器打开；正式日历邀请可进入日程。支持已读／未读切换、全部已读、移到回收站及恢复；默认仅在本机整理，可在邮件设置中开启「同步邮件操作到邮箱」。 支持 **QQ、163、126、腾讯企业邮、iCloud、Gmail 和自定义 IMAP**。验证码可设置在 30／60／300 秒后自动隐藏，覆盖列表、正文与通知；主动查看后会再次隐藏。 ## AI 还剩多少额度，抬眼就知道 ![AI 额度面板：Codex 额度、WorkBuddy 积分与 DeepSeek 余额](docs/images/readme/ai-quota.webp) 支持 **Codex、Claude、Kimi、Grok Bot、Gemini、ZCode、WorkBuddy、DeepSeek 和 Kiro**。 订阅额度、重置时间、套餐积分与 API 余额，按服务展示。多个账号可分别命名、选择配色，常用账号直接放在收起的小岛上。 - **ZCode**：查看套餐额度。 - **Claude**：只读取桌面版本地用量历史与缓存，或接收 Claude Code 官方状态栏输出；岛仔不使用 Claude 登录令牌，也不请求 Claude 额度接口。数据随官方客户端使用更新，桌面版缓存有效时自动显示重置时间，读取不到时显示未知。 - **Kiro**：只读识别 Kiro 登录缓存并核验用户，显示套餐、有效试用与赠送 / 加购点数及明细，超额上限单独显示；支持美国东部和欧洲中部区域。不自动续期，登录过期时请在 Kiro 中重新登录。 - **WorkBuddy**：查看剩余积分；优先识别本机客户端登录，也可在默认浏览器完成授权。 - **Gemini**：支持 Chrome 144+ 原生授权连接，读取官网的 5 小时与每周额度，无需扩展。先在 Chrome 登录 Gemini，首次在 `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` 开启连接，回岛仔点击连接并在 Chrome 允许授权；会话加密保存在本机，后续独立刷新。高级设置保留手动 Cookie 连接。 - **DeepSeek**：使用 API Key 连接，查看账户余额、充值与赠送金额。 - **中转站**：自动识别通用余额、New API 和 Sub2API，保留 One API 兼容计费接口；New API 可用用户 Token 查询账户余额。高级设置支持粘贴 CC Switch 的 `request` / `extractor` 自定义查询脚本，脚本与凭据加密保存在本机。 连接方式、可用字段与账号订阅有关；请求失败或登录过期时，以对应服务的官方页面为准。 ## 出门前先看一眼天气 天气页显示当前实况与未来七天预报：温度、天气现象、体感、湿度、风速、日出日落时间，以及每天的最高／最低温和降水概率。 - Everything is done in one of three places: - **the board**, in your browser, for you; - **MCP**, for your agents: they take tasks, move cards and comment; - **the `kanzo` command**, for the terminal and scripts. ## Install > [!TIP] > **Just ask your agent:** *"install Kanzo from github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo."* ```sh curl -LsSf https://github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo/releases/latest/download/kanzo-installer.sh | sh ``` For macOS and Linux, including every Raspberry Pi. On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo/releases/latest/download/kanzo-installer.ps1 | iex" ``` Both add Kanzo to your `PATH`, for terminals you open from then on. To use it in the one you installed from, run `source $HOME/.cargo/env` (`env.fish` in fish), or open a new one. Or download the Windows zip from the [latest release](https://github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo/releases/latest) and put `kanzo.exe` in a folder named `bin` on your `PATH`, like `%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin`: the board updates itself only there. Every release is signed by GitHub: check a download with `gh attestation verify --repo emanuele-em/kanzo`. Or with Cargo: ```sh cargo install kanzo ``` ## Start > [!TIP] > **Just ask your agent:** *"start Kanzo and keep it running at login."* ```sh kanzo ``` The board opens at http://localhost:4242. That's all the setup there is: the first run creates `~/kanzo`, and the whole board lives in it. | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | `n` | New task | | `/` or `⌘K` | Search every project | | `f` | Filter the board; `↵` keeps the filter | | `Tab` | Move to the description | | `⌘↵` | Save and close | | `Esc` | Keep what you typed in a description or tags; cancel other fields | ## Use the board > [!TIP] > **Just ask your agent:** *"mark kanzo#12 as human, and set its URL to github.com/acme/api/pull/482."* - **Select tasks:** `⌘`-click them, or drag on empty board space, then move, tag or delete them together. Drag one and the rest follow. - **List view:** the list icon shows the same tasks as rows to sort and group. - **Human tasks:** mark a task Human and agents leave it to you. The person icon shows only those. - **Images:** paste or drop one into a task or a comment. - **Links:** give a task a URL, like its pull request, and open it from its card. On macOS, `kanzo` then opens it instead of a tab, on the default port. - **Updates:** when a new version is out, the sidebar offers it. # WowType **在 Linux 上打字，像微信输入法一样顺手。** 一个 fcitx5 拼音输入法：长句一次打完、打一半就有词、按错键也能认出来，越用越懂你。 [![CI](https://github.com/Gloridust/WowType/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Gloridust/WowType/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Gloridust/WowType?include_prereleases&label=release)](https://github.com/Gloridust/WowType/releases) ![fcitx5](https://img.shields.io/badge/fcitx5-%E2%89%A5%205.0-blue) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2F%20Apache--2.0-green) [安装](#安装) · [使用](#使用) · [设置](#设置) · [更多文档](#更多文档) · [常见问题](#常见问题) · [工作原理](#工作原理) · [参与开发](#参与开发) [![加入 Telegram 交流群](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E5%8A%A0%E5%85%A5%20Telegram%20%E4%BA%A4%E6%B5%81%E7%BE%A4-26A5E4?style=for-the-badge&logo=telegram&logoColor=white)](https://t.me/+Kxk-4VkXIS9lODM1)
介绍视频 v0.3.12：互译、语音输入、macOS 版、日期时间、候选更准……
## 特性


候选横排，和微信输入法一样：整句只留几个，后面是词，最后是单字

- **整句输入**：`xiangquzijieshangban` 直接出「想去字节上班」；后面跟着句子的前半截，可以先上屏一段，剩下的拼音接着改。自带 WowType 自己训的整句增强模型（字级神经语言模型），长句的首选更准，开箱即用；也可以导入微信输入法的（[说明](docs/CONFIG.md#数据文件)）。 - **半成品也有词**：`zhongg` 就有「中国」，不用打全。打全了的拼音正好是个词时，它一定排第一。 - **按错键能认出来**：按成相邻键、两个键按反、多按或漏按一个键（`zhognguo` → 中国）。本来就打对的输入不受影响。 - **越用越懂你**：记住你选过的词和常连着用的词（选过一次「我们再讨论」，下次就不会出「我们在讨论」），30 天不用会慢慢淡掉。 - **简拼、省略韵母、中英混打**：`bjdx` → 北京大学；有的音节只打声母也行，`kyi` → 可以、`yongzwen` → 用中文；zh/ch/sh 可以当一个声母，`zhch`、`zhchi` → 支持；`github` → GitHub。 - **候选横排**，和微信输入法一样：整句只留几个，后面是词，最后是单字。 - **语音输入**：按住右 `Alt` 说话，松开就上屏；也可以点一下右 `Alt` 说，说完停一下自动结束。用微信输入法的离线识别模型，在本机识别，不上传录音。 - **Emoji**：打「开心」「点赞」「生日快乐」时，第三个候选就是对应的 emoji；按 `Super` + `.` 打开表情面板，打拼音或英文搜 emoji 和符号（`xiao` → 😂、`pizza` → 🍕、`youjiantou` → →）。 - **互译**：单按 `Shift` 切到「译」，照常打中文，停一下就翻成英文（或日、韩、法等 13 种语言），回车上屏；打外文就翻成中文。可以下载腾讯混元的 HY-MT 翻译模型离线翻，可以用哔哩哔哩免费的 Index-Translate（不用注册、不用 API Key），也可以填你自己的 OpenAI 格式接口（DeepSeek、通义千问、Ollama……）。 - **日期时间、计算器**：打 `riqi`（`rq`）、`shijian`（`sj`）、`xingqi`，首选后面就是今天的日期、现在的时间（`2026年11月10日`、`2026-11-10`、`15:52`……）；`v1+2*3` 直接出 `7`；只打一个数（`v12345.67`）出大写金额「壹万贰仟叁佰肆拾伍元陆角柒分」和「一万二千三百四十五点六七」。双拼时 `v` 是声母键，计算器用大写 `V`（`V1+2*3`）。 - **v + 空格工具栏**：只打一个 `v` 再按空格，选剪贴板历史（默认关，最近 20 条，只在内存里）、常用语（自定义词）、符号、表情。 - **中英文之间自动加空格**（默认关）：`你好Linux` → `你好 Linux`、`第5章` → `第 5 章`，字母和数字分别开关。 - **繁体、模糊音、双拼**：可切繁体输出；模糊音分 16 组单独开（z=zh、n=l、f=h、r=l、an=ang、un=ong、huang=wang……）；双拼支持自然码、小鹤、微软、搜狗、智能 ABC、紫光、拼音加加，双拼也有整句、句首词和分段选词，编辑区显示全拼。 - **五笔 86**：设置里「输入方案」选「五笔输入」。四码唯一自动上屏、第五码顶字、标点顶字、空码提示，候选后面显示还要打的码；不会打的字按 `z` 临时打拼音，候选后面就是它的五笔码。码表来自 [rime-wubi](https://github.com/rime/rime-wubi)，码位固定、不调频，见[五笔](#五笔)。 - **图形设置界面**：候选排列、模糊音、语音键都在「WowType 设置」里点一下就改，马上生效；还能加自定义词（人名、公司名、常用的长句、邮箱），加进去的词排第一，简拼也能打；编码可以是 `mail` 这类字母，词里能换行，可以导入导出。 - **打字统计**（默认关）：在设置的「统计」页打开后，看今天和累计的输入字数、活跃时长、速度、连续天数，以及每个键按了多少次（按键热力图）和候选命中位置。只在本机按天记计数，不记打的字、拼音、按键顺序和时刻，密码框里的不算；随时可以清除，见 [docs/CONFIG.md](docs/CONFIG.md#打字统计)。 - **快、全在本地**：完整的雾凇拼音词库，按一个键一般几毫秒内出候选；不联网，输入内容不离开你的电脑（语音模型在设置里下载一次；在线互译只在切到「译」时把那句话发给你选的服务）。

长句一口气打完
还能只上屏前半截「想去字节」，剩下的接着选
按错顺序，没关系
weixni 照样是「微信」

全简拼混打，也没问题
wanqky → 完全可以
中英混打，不用切换
wechat → WeChat，大小写按词表来

打着字，顺手就有表情
第三个候选是「开心😊」，选了上屏「今天好开心😊」
按住右 Alt 说话
离线识别，录音不上传

content.readme: # ZigZag **[Visit zigzag.diy](https://zigzag.diy/)** ZigZag is a visual embroidery editor built in Rust for performance, with built-in **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** support so AI agents can create and edit designs alongside you. Turn SVG artwork into stitches, fine-tune it in the editor, and export **PES, DST, EXP, JEF, or VP3** for broad compatibility with embroidery machines—or send designs directly to a **Brother Skitch (PP1) over Bluetooth**. Draw in Illustrator, draw in ZigZag, or let an agent draw. The Rust engine and `zigzag` command-line tool power the same workflow outside the editor. ## See ZigZag in action https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94812f25-82f4-429f-85db-5e20c1d5e723 **Stitching on a Brother Skitch (PP1)** [Download the video (MP4, 1080p)](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/raw/refs/heads/main/packaging/media/skitch-pp1-demo.mp4) · [Original post on X](https://x.com/simpsoka/status/2115254318161182876). ## Download for Mac **[Download ZigZag.dmg](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/releases/latest/download/ZigZag.dmg)** For Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or later. Open the DMG, then drag ZigZag into Applications. The release is signed and notarized by Apple. No Rust installation is needed. Or with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh): ```sh brew install --cask simpsoka/zigzag/zigzag ``` To update a Homebrew installation: ```sh brew upgrade --cask --greedy simpsoka/zigzag/zigzag ``` Starting with version 0.1.3, ZigZag also offers an in-app updater: it tells you when there's a newer release and installs it when you say (ZigZag › Check for Updates…). ## Download for Windows **[Download ZigZag for Windows](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/releases/latest)** — the `ZigZag--x86_64-windows.zip` asset on the latest release. For 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1709 or later) and Windows 11. Unzip it and double-click **ZigZag.exe**. Windows SmartScreen warns on apps without a Microsoft-trusted signature the first time they run; click *More info* → *Run anyway*. No Rust installation is needed. ## Download for Linux **[Download ZigZag for Linux](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/releases/latest)** — the `ZigZag--x86_64-linux.tar.gz` asset on the latest release. For x86-64 Linux desktops with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+), X11 or Wayland, and OpenGL. Extract the archive and run `./zigzag-studio` inside the extracted folder. It also includes the `zigzag` CLI and `zigzag-mcp` bridge; no Rust installation is needed. See the included `README.txt` for runtime dependencies and Bluetooth setup. [Release notes and checksums](https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag/releases/latest) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Publishing a release](RELEASE.md) ``` zigzag/ src/svg.rs SVG import (usvg): fill and stroke parts, transforms, text src/document/ editable document; settings saved back into SVG ids, layout edits as SVG transforms, lettering src/params.rs stitch settings tokens + fabric presets src/stitch/fill.rs tatami fill (scanline sections, staggered rows) src/stitch/satin.rs satin columns: two rails, auto-satin, underlays, short stitches, lean src/stitch/cat.rs letters into satin columns by their chordal axis (strokes, joins, mitres) src/stitch/columns.rs shapes that branch or have holes, cut into satin columns (`cut`) src/stitch/stroke.rs running / triple-run stitch src/boolean.rs polygon booleans and offsets (i_overlay) src/design.rs planner: overlap removal, cap order, routing, trims src/route.rs travel out of sight: a way through fills and under what covers src/checks.rs digitizing checks (sizes, widths, lettering, hoop) src/machine/profile.rs machine profiles: hoops and file format, built in (profiles.json) or your own src/formats/ PES (+PEC), DST, EXP, JEF, VP3, Skitch PEN writers; PES/PEC/DST/EXP/JEF readers; preview; worksheet src/machine/ Skitch Bluetooth protocol (+ btleplug client, `ble` feature) src/studio/ editor (egui on OpenGL via glow) + MCP server (`gui` feature) src/mcp_bridge.rs stdio ↔ HTTP bridge for MCP clients that launch a command ``` ## Build ```sh cargo build --release # CLI + MCP bridge, no system deps cargo build --release --features gui,ble # + the studio editor and Skitch upload ``` Linux needs the usual X11/Wayland and OpenGL dev libraries for `gui`. libdbus is vendored for `ble`. ## Stitch types | Type | What it does | Works on |
